ov: A great ape of the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa and, with the bonobo, humanity’s closest living relative. Chimpanzees live in communities that can top 200 members, split into smaller foraging parties by day.

why.dg: Attacks by wild great apes are rare, but chimpanzees are the most likely to attack, mostly children, near forest edges and farmland.

rg: Forests and savannas across equatorial Africa.
df: Mainly fruit, plus leaves, seeds, flowers, bark and resin, insects and honey, and sometimes meat from hunting.

cf.tip: A bonobo has longer limbs, a darker face, pink lips and long hair parted on its head, and is consistently smaller.

fx: Some chimpanzees make sharpened sticks and use them to spear small mammals.
